projects.sectionIntro: Seven projects taken from concept to production, for clients in tourism, real estate and graphic design. Each solved a concrete problem rather than just changing how a page looks.
projects.p1Desc: Custom web solution for the Sottomonte agency: Building a high-performance responsive system. Advanced SEO optimization and a custom layout designed for maximum conversion and loading speed.
projects.p2Desc: Custom web solution for presenting premium accommodation on the Pelješac peninsula. System designed focusing on visual content loading speed and responsive design ensuring ease of booking on all devices.
projects.p3Desc: Sabioncello: From design concept to a complete destination guide. Development of a modern and scalable web solution optimized for an international audience, with emphasis on visual storytelling and technical SEO excellence.
projects.p4Desc: Sabioncello Grafika: A modern web application for graphic design services, built in React. A scalable design ecosystem emphasizing visual presentation, contemporary UX, and technical excellence.
projects.p5Desc: Dani Cvjetnog: A custom web solution for a student event. Interactive sign-up forms for games and clear event information, designed for easy navigation and a smooth visitor experience.
projects.p4MetaTitle: Sabioncello Grafika: React app for a graphic design studio
projects.p4MetaDesc: A React web application for graphic design studio Sabioncello Grafika: fast, responsive presentation of services and a modern user experience.
projects.p4Intro: Sabioncello Grafika is a graphic design studio that needed a digital presence matching its own visual standard. Rather than a conventional brochure site, the project was built as a React application, fast, modular, and easy to extend with new services.
projects.p4Challenge: A studio whose business is visual identity cannot afford a generic website. Two things that usually pull against each other had to be reconciled: rich visual presentation of the work, and load speed on mobile, where most visits arrive. The service offering also changes, so the structure had to absorb new content without a redesign.
projects.p4Approach: The application was built in React with Vite, using a component structure where each service is a separate, reusable element. Images are optimised and served in modern formats, and the layout was developed mobile-first. Particular attention went to typography and white space, keeping the studio’s work in the foreground and the interface out of the way.
projects.p4F1: Component-based React architecture that absorbs new services without design changes
projects.p4F2: Mobile-first responsive layout tested across a wide range of screen sizes
projects.p4F3: Optimised imagery and minimal JavaScript for fast loading
projects.p4F4: Clean typographic hierarchy that keeps the visual work in focus
projects.p4Delivered: A production application was delivered on its own domain, ready for further content expansion, with a documented code structure for future changes.
projects.p1MetaTitle: Sottomonte: WordPress website for a real estate agency
projects.p1MetaDesc: A WordPress website for real estate agency Sottomonte: a clear property catalogue, technical SEO groundwork and fast page loads.
projects.p1Intro: Sottomonte is a real estate agency that needed a site taking two things seriously: a clear presentation of its listings, and visibility in search. The solution was built on WordPress so the client could maintain listings independently.
projects.p1Challenge: Property listings change constantly, so editing content could not depend on a developer. At the same time, property pages are image-heavy, which easily destroys load speed, and speed together with technical SEO decides whether the listings get found at all.
projects.p1Approach: WordPress was set up with a content structure tailored to properties and templates that hold a consistent layout regardless of who enters the data. On the technical side the SEO groundwork was implemented: a semantic heading hierarchy, meta data, optimised images and a clean URL scheme. The layout was developed responsively, with emphasis on browsing listings on a phone.
projects.p1F1: Independent listing management through WordPress, with no developer in the loop
projects.p1F2: Technical SEO groundwork: semantic headings, meta data and clean URLs
projects.p1F3: Optimised property imagery for fast loading over mobile networks
projects.p1F4: Responsive layout tuned for browsing the catalogue on a phone
projects.p1Delivered: The site went live on its own domain, handed over with documentation for entering and maintaining content.
projects.p2MetaTitle: Visit Eva Orebić: website for tourist accommodation on Pelješac
projects.p2MetaDesc: A WordPress site for Visit Eva accommodation in Orebić: visual presentation, fast-loading galleries and a straightforward booking contact.
projects.p2Intro: Visit Eva Orebić presents private accommodation in Orebić on the Pelješac peninsula. The goal was for a guest to get a clear picture of the property and its surroundings within seconds, and to find the booking contact without hunting for it.
projects.p2Challenge: Tourism content is almost entirely visual, large photo galleries are essential, yet they are also the heaviest load on page speed. On top of that, much of the traffic arrives from mobile devices and from abroad, often on slower networks where every unnecessary second is felt directly.
projects.p2Approach: Photographs were processed and served at optimised sizes, with galleries below the fold loaded lazily. The page structure walks the visitor through linearly: the accommodation, its amenities, the surroundings, then contact. WordPress was configured so the owner can refresh photos and seasonal information without technical knowledge.
projects.p2F1: Optimised galleries with lazy loading below the fold
projects.p2F2: Linear structure that guides the visitor toward the booking contact
projects.p2F3: Seasonal content updates without technical knowledge
projects.p2F4: Responsive presentation suited to guests searching from a phone
projects.p2Delivered: The site was published on its own domain and handed over with instructions for seasonal content maintenance.
projects.p3MetaTitle: Sabioncello: destination web guide for the Pelješac peninsula
projects.p3MetaDesc: A destination web guide for Pelješac: content architecture for an international audience, visual storytelling and technical SEO.
projects.p3Intro: Sabioncello is a destination guide for the Pelješac peninsula, aimed primarily at international visitors. The project started from a design concept and grew into a complete content system.
projects.p3Challenge: A destination guide poses a different problem from a presentation site: there is a lot of content and it has to stay findable. Visitors arrive with different intentions, beaches, wine, accommodation, activities, so the structure has to absorb growth without becoming unnavigable. The audience is international, which places demands on both language and load speed from abroad.
projects.p3Approach: Content was organised into clear thematic sections with consistent templates, so every new page automatically inherits the correct heading structure and internal linking. Technical SEO was treated as part of the architecture rather than a later addition: semantic headings, descriptive URLs and optimised images. The visual language leans on landscape photography with restrained typography.
projects.p3F1: Thematic content architecture that scales with the number of pages
projects.p3F2: Internal linking that carries visitors through related topics
projects.p3F3: Technical SEO built into the templates rather than bolted on
projects.p3F4: Visual storytelling built on destination photography
projects.p3Delivered: The guide was published and structured so new destinations and topics can be added without further development work.
projects.p5MetaTitle: Dani Cvjetnog: website for a student event
projects.p5MetaDesc: A website for the Dani Cvjetnog student event: programme overview, interactive sign-up forms and instant loading with no CMS.
projects.p5Intro: Dani Cvjetnog is a student event that needed a simple site carrying the programme and sign-ups for its games. Given the short-lived purpose and the need for speed, it was built without a CMS, plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
projects.p5Challenge: Event sites have highly concentrated traffic: most visits happen in the few days before the event, largely from mobile devices. The site had to be instantly available with no database dependency, and the sign-ups simple enough to complete on the first attempt.
projects.p5Approach: The site was written as a static set of files, which removed an entire layer of things that can fail in production. Sign-up forms were implemented in JavaScript with client-side validation and clear error messages. The programme is laid out for legibility on a small screen.
projects.p5F1: Static build with no database, a minimal surface for failure
projects.p5F2: Interactive sign-up forms with validation and clear error messages
projects.p5F3: Programme layout readable on a mobile screen
projects.p5F4: Instant loading thanks to the absence of a CMS layer
projects.p5Delivered: The site was published ahead of the event and used throughout the programme.
projects.p6Subtitle: Website for a campsite on Pelješac
projects.p6Desc: Camping Lovište Paradise: a single-page React application for a family-run campsite in Lovište bay. Presentation of the pitches and facilities, a multilingual interface, and a clear path to a booking enquiry.
projects.p6MetaTitle: Camping Lovište Paradise: website for a campsite on Pelješac
projects.p6MetaDesc: A React website for Camping Lovište Paradise: presenting the terraced pitches, the camp facilities and the surrounding area, with a multilingual interface and an enquiry form.
projects.p6Intro: Camping Lovište Paradise is a family-run campsite in Lovište bay on the western tip of the Pelješac peninsula. It needed a site that explains to an international guest, within seconds, what the camp is like, what it offers and how to book, without burying them in detail.
projects.p6Challenge: A campsite is chosen visually, but the decision is made on specifics: what the sanitary block is like, whether there is shade, how far the sea is, whether pets are allowed. A large amount of practical information had to sit alongside a presentation that stays calm and easy to scan. The audience is mostly international and arrives on mobile, usually while still planning the trip.
projects.p6Approach: The site was built as a single-page React application with Vite, split into clear sections: a sense of the location, the camp facilities, the sanitary block, activities in the area, and distances to nearby places. The content is multilingual, and the photography is organised into galleries that load progressively. Every section ends with a clear route to the enquiry form.
projects.p6F1: Single-page React architecture with clearly separated thematic sections
projects.p6F2: Multilingual interface for guests arriving from different countries
projects.p6F3: Photo galleries of the camp, the sanitary block and the surroundings, loaded progressively
projects.p6F4: Distances to nearby destinations and a map, for easier trip planning
projects.p6Delivered: The site was published on its own domain, structured so content and seasonal information can be added without development work.
projects.p7Desc: BMFit: a conversion-focused landing page for personal trainer Benjamin Matošević. It walks the visitor from the problem to a sign-up, with a clear account of the programme and answers to common objections.
projects.p7MetaTitle: BMFit: landing page for a fitness coaching programme
projects.p7MetaDesc: A landing page for the BMFit coaching programme: a structure that carries the visitor from problem to sign-up, loading instantly with no CMS layer.
projects.p7Intro: BMFit is Benjamin Matošević’s personal training programme, aimed at women who have started and stopped several times before. The page has a single job: explain why the previous attempts failed, and turn that recognition into a sign-up.
projects.p7Challenge: A single-goal landing page misses more easily than a full website. The visitor arrives sceptical, often after a bad experience, and leaves within seconds if they do not recognise their own situation. The order of the argument had to be arranged so each section answers the question the previous one raises, without tipping into a hard sell.
projects.p7Approach: The page was built as a static set of files with no CMS, which gives it instant loading and a minimal surface for failure. The content is sequenced as an argument: the problem, the cause, a three-step system, who runs the programme, and answers to common questions, with every section leading back to the same sign-up form. The visual language is a dark ground with a single accent tone, so the calls to action stay unmistakable.
projects.p7F1: Static build with no CMS, loading instantly
projects.p7F2: Content sequenced as an argument, from problem through to sign-up
projects.p7F3: Three-step programme breakdown and a frequently-asked-questions section
projects.p7F4: Consistent calls to action all leading to the same sign-up form
projects.p7Delivered: The page was published on its own domain, with a simple structure that allows the offer to be revised and new messaging tested without development work.
